payload.instructions: Preserve all candidate IDs and distinctions. Broader parent themes organize evidence; they do not imply measurement equivalence.

themes.disagreements: contradictions, weak signals, and proxy distinctions
evidence_ids: at most 12 representative supplied modeling evidence IDs
themes.interpretation: common or complementary evidence
themes.name: theme

themes.disagreements: Pemetrexed displays strong confounding and modification signals, whereas MET amplification is primarily an effect modifier with minimal impact on treatment selection.
themes.interpretation: Molecular targets and chemotherapy markers providing strong evidence for treatment heterogeneity.
themes.name: Tumor Molecular Markers

themes.disagreements: Metastasis location is a strong confounder and modifier; FLAIR hyperintensity is a modest modifier; meningeal thickening is primarily prognostic with weak signals elsewhere.
themes.interpretation: Radiological markers of disease extent and location.
themes.name: Neuro-Radiological Findings

themes.disagreements: Metabolic response is a credible effect modifier; mucositis is primarily prognostic without strong evidence for confounding or modification.
themes.interpretation: Markers of clinical and physiological response status.
themes.name: Clinical and Metabolic Status

themes.disagreements: High consistency across all model families for both prognosis and interaction, though permutation importance in predictive forests is lower than the strong univariable and causal forest signals.
themes.interpretation: Strong systemic inflammatory marker showing robust evidence for both confounding (outcome prognosis) and effect modification (treatment heterogeneity).
themes.name: Systemic Inflammation

themes.disagreements: Variable signal strength across symptoms; neurological symptoms and nausea show stronger interaction evidence (Causal Forest, R-learner) compared to night sweats and necrotic fluid.
themes.interpretation: Cluster of pretreatment symptomatic indicators exhibiting evidence for both treatment prediction and heterogeneity of effect.
themes.name: Clinical Symptomatology

themes.disagreements: Napsin A expression shows strong interaction evidence, whereas N-stage and NSCLC diagnosis signals are considerably weaker and less consistent across folds.
themes.interpretation: Pathological and staging markers where Napsin A is a credible effect modifier, and N-stage potentially serves as both a confounder and modifier.
themes.name: Disease Pathology and Stage

themes.disagreements: Evidence is primarily driven by predictive forests; univariable signals are weak or absent for MI presence.
themes.interpretation: General health indicators and comorbidities with moderate predictive signals, though myelosuppression exhibits more credible evidence for a dual role.
themes.name: General Health and Comorbidities

themes.disagreements: Causal forest support for effect modification is low for both (26% for OA, 20% for osteopenia), confirming their roles as primarily confounders rather than effect modifiers.
themes.interpretation: High-confidence signals for both treatment assignment and outcome prognosis, suggesting a strong confounding role.
themes.name: Bone Density and Musculoskeletal Comorbidities

themes.disagreements: Optic chiasm enhancement shows strong prognostic (66%) and interaction (53%) signals, whereas optic nerve enhancement signals are weak and inconsistent across models.
themes.interpretation: Radiological signals associated with the optic pathway showing a blend of prognostic importance and treatment-heterogeneity evidence.
themes.name: Optic Pathway Imaging Enhancement

themes.disagreements: NYHA class is primarily an effect modifier (60% Causal Forest), while organomegaly is a stronger predictor of treatment (60%) and outcome (73%), marking it as a confounder.
themes.interpretation: Indicators of overall patient health and organ involvement, demonstrating either strong prognosis or effect modification.
themes.name: Systemic Clinical and Functional Status

themes.disagreements: While some features show moderate predictive forest support, these are not replicated across other model families and lack the strength to justify a specific role.
themes.interpretation: General patient characteristics and clinical status with insufficient or contradictory evidence to establish a causal role.
themes.name: Demographic and Operational Factors

themes.disagreements: Oxygen saturation (241) shows extremely strong univariable signals, whereas oxygen therapy use (242) has more modest p-values.
themes.interpretation: Patients with lower oxygen saturation and the use of supplemental oxygen are strongly associated with both treatment assignment and outcome prognosis.
themes.name: Respiratory Status and Oxygenation

themes.disagreements: Palliative care status (246) is a very strong prognostic factor (p=0.002), while documented wishes (247) primarily predict treatment assignment.
themes.interpretation: Palliative care status and the documentation of patient wishes act as markers for both treatment selection and prognosis, often reflecting severity of illness.
themes.name: Care Preferences and End-of-Life Status

themes.disagreements: Both show weak univariable effect signals but maintain support in Causal Forest models.
themes.interpretation: PD-L1 and p40 expression show support in causal forests, suggesting they may modify the treatment effect.
themes.name: Tumor Biomarkers

themes.disagreements: Pain severity (245) is a strong outcome predictor (p=0.002), while specific drug doses (244, 249) lack strong univariable evidence.
themes.interpretation: Pain severity and neuropathy grades are primarily prognostic factors for the outcome, while dose measurements show minimal consistent signal.
themes.name: Symptom Burden and Therapy Dosing

themes.disagreements: Pituitary-specific features (255, 256, 257) lack significant support across multiple model families compared to peritumoral edema and periventricular signal abnormality.
themes.interpretation: Features describing structural or signal abnormalities on neuroimaging, exhibiting varied degrees of prognostic and heterogeneity signals.
themes.name: Brain Radiographic Findings

themes.disagreements: Phospho-MET status (253) shows support only in the R-learner for effect modification, while PI3K activation (254) is supported by the Causal Forest, providing more robust evidence for the latter.
themes.interpretation: Biomarkers related to intracellular signaling pathways and receptor phosphorylation status.
themes.name: Molecular Signaling

themes.disagreements: Platelet count shows a dominant treatment prediction signal (univariable) compared to the outcome-dominant signals of pleural effusion and pneumonia.
themes.interpretation: General systemic markers including hematological counts and clinical diagnoses that may reflect overall patient fragility or comorbidities.
themes.name: Systemic Health and Clinical Status

themes.disagreements: Signals for posterior fossa features are generally weaker than for primary tumor or systemic indicators, appearing primarily in forest-based models rather than univariable or penalized models.
themes.interpretation: Posterior fossa imaging features (enhancement and mass effect) show complementary signals across treatment prediction and outcome prognosis, with modest evidence for effect modification in causal forests.
themes.name: Posterior Fossa Imaging

themes.disagreements: Treatment and outcome signals are inconsistent across models, while the causal forest provides a more stable signal for effect modification, particularly for location.
themes.interpretation: Primary tumor physical characteristics (location, morphology, and size) consistently show signals for effect modification and variable levels of prognostic/predictive importance.
themes.name: Primary Tumor Physicality

system:
You review pretreatment candidate measurements using modeling evidence
from one outer-training fold. First identify themes across candidates; then
reconcile their roles as confounder, effect_modifier, both, or neither.
All evidence is fallible. No individual family, p-value, or support frequency is
a hard selection gate. A credible complementary signal can justify retention
even when other methods shrink it away. Do not mistake correlated aliases or
proxies for multiple independent discoveries. Themes organize evidence; they
do not establish equivalence, merge measurements, or transfer a role to every
theme member. Preserve investigator-locked roles exactly.

Treatment prediction, outcome prognosis, and confounding are distinct. Discuss
whether a candidate could be a common cause rather than an instrument or only a
prognostic factor. Effect modification needs treatment-heterogeneity evidence;
outcome main-effect importance alone does not establish it. Univariable logistic
interactions are on the log-odds scale and unadjusted for other covariates.
Orthogonal linear models, candidate R-learners, and causal forests assess the
probability/outcome scale after elastic-net nuisance adjustment. Their targets
and biases differ. A model family is evidence, not an independent replication.

Use exposure and evaluability denominators. Missing or nonconverged fits are not
negative votes. Repeated samples and folds overlap; support fractions are not
causal probabilities or formal stability-selection error guarantees. Raw and BH
p-values do not correct the upstream adaptive discovery process. Permutation
importance can be diluted by correlated alternatives and does not prove a
causal role. Compare fold consistency, methods, subsets, and conflicting facts.
Definitions and theme names cannot establish a role without the supplied
empirical evidence. Never invent an oracle, data-generating process, or hidden
truth. Return the requested JSON and cite only supplied evidence IDs.
